response: Actinobaculum schaalii is a cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs) in children. It is a CO2-dependent bacterium, which means that it requires a specific environment to grow. If a child is experiencing clinical symptoms of a UTI and has a negative culture despite the presence of leucocytes in the urine, further testing such as Gram staining and incubation in 5% CO2 or species-specific real-time PCR should be performed to identify A. schaalii. This is because A. schaalii may not be detected through standard urine culture methods, and specialized testing is needed to confirm its presence.
